subject: [Escalation] Nimbus Retail: v4.2 quant rollout — p95 latency spike & failures
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@nimbusretail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:32:14 -0800
Subject: Noticeable latency + error spike after v4.2/quant rollout

Monica —

We pushed the model update you recommended (v4.2 with qprofile v2-beta) to our production inference pool at 03:10 PDT this morning and immediately saw a large jump in p95 latency and an uptick in request errors. Quick summary from our side:

- p50: +10ms (expected)
- p95: +420ms (was 210ms historically)
- Error rate: increased from ~0.2% to 1.8% (5xx and decode errors)
- Throughput: stable, but tail latency is causing timeouts in our API layer

We attached a small sample of raw logs and a screenshot of our SLO dashboard. This is impacting our checkout flow during peak times — we are already seeing a 6% drop in conversion on the redo path. Our legal/procurement team is copying in procurement@nimbusretail.com for record.

We need a triage and rollback plan. If this is a known regression tied to the quant profile, please confirm rollback steps and ETA.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Director of Platform Engineering
Nimbus Retail

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:07:58 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Noticeable latency + error spike after v4.2/quant rollout

On the call now with infra/ops. Preliminary findings:
- The v4.2 model + qprofile v2-beta increases KV cache churn on our GPU runtime for sequences > 512 tokens, which forces more cross-device synchronization at higher tail percentiles.
- An optimization in the new kernel path (memory staging) appears to push some decode paths into a slower fallback that increases tail latency; that's generating intermittent 5xx decode timeouts.

Immediate mitigation options being worked by infra:
1) Route Nimbus traffic to the v4.2 qprofile stable-compat (older quant) and mark qprofile v2-beta paused for their tenant. Target: revert traffic within 45–90 minutes.
2) If option (1) is unavailable due to provisioning, roll back model to v4.1 for Nimbus temporarily; target: 2–3 hours.

Irene is collecting a short RCA draft and will push a hotfix plan if the kernel fallback is confirmed. I'll update the customer in the triage.

–Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:31:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Noticeable latency + error spike after v4.2/quant rollout — immediate plan

Alex —

Thanks for the quick confirmation on the call. Short update and plan:

- Root cause hypothesis: qprofile v2-beta + v4.2 triggers a kernel path that increases KV cache churn and causes tail decode fallbacks for longer sequences.
- Immediate action: We will route your production traffic back to the stable qprofile (v1.9) for Nimbus and pause v2-beta for your tenant. Estimated in-flight rollback window: ~60 minutes.
- If the stable qprofile does not fully restore p95 to your SLA target, we will proceed with model rollback to v4.1 as fallback (additional 1–2 hours).

We will:
- Post a short incident update in this thread when rollback begins and when complete.
- Share an RCA draft within 48 hours and a permanent mitigation plan (kernel fix + improved qprofile gating) within 7 business days.

Apologies again — we understand the business impact and will prioritize credits/SLAs if this crosses the SLA threshold. I will keep Rishi and Vivek looped on any request for exec outreach or formal remediation.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:05:49 -0800
Subject: Re: Noticeable latency + error spike after v4.2/quant rollout — exec summary

Team / Alex —

Quick executive summary after the rollback window:
- Timeline: rollback to stable qprofile (v1.9) completed 2026-11-15 11:10 PDT. Customer p95 improved from ~630ms at peak to ~220ms within 30 minutes. Error rate returned to baseline by 11:45 PDT.
- Impact: transient revenue impact estimated at ~1.2% over the incident window (internal estimate from Nimbus logs).
- Root cause (draft): a kernel memory-staging optimization on v4.2 exposed a quantization interaction that increases KV cache churn for sequences > 512; this surfaced at high concurrency and caused decode fallbacks.
- Actions taken: rollback qprofile for Nimbus, paused v2-beta rollout for accounts in the same tier, issued internal ticket to engineering for a kernel-level fix and additional qprofile gating in the release pipeline.
- Customer ask: formal RCA, timeline for permanent fix, and discussion of SLA remediation.

Next steps (owners):
- Irene: technical RCA + hotfix plan (ETA 48 hours).
- Monica/Priyom: prepare customer-facing RCA and postmortem; propose SLA credit if requested (Rishi to approve).
- Rishi/Vivek: if Nimbus requests exec engagement, schedule a short CTO/VP call this week.

I'll mark this as high priority and stand by for the RCA. Good job triaging quickly.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
